dashboard.label: Cluster Colors
dashboard.description: Per-clusterGroup color configuration added in v4.5.1. All panels use makeresults — no external data needed.

html.p: Assign distinct colors to named marker cluster groups using the clusterGroupColors formatter option, per-row SPL fields, or both together. Count labels automatically switch to white on dark backgrounds.

tr.td: Comma-separated groupName:color pairs. Supports hex, rgba(), and named CSS colors. Use the reserved key default as a catch-all for group names not explicitly listed.
Per-row override for the outer ring color of this row's clusterGroup. Takes priority over clusterGroupColors. If only one SPL color field is present the other mirrors it.
Per-row override for the inner circle color of this row's clusterGroup. Takes priority over clusterGroupColors.

html.p: Resolution order: SPL fields ➜ clusterGroupColors[groupName] ➜ clusterGroupColors[default] ➜ threshold fallback (green / yellow / orange).
Alpha: Hex and named colors automatically derive a 0.6-opacity outer ring and 0.8-opacity inner circle. rgba() values use your alpha as-is.
Set clusterGroupColors in the Formatter to assign a fixed color to each group. Your SPL only needs to output the clusterGroup field — no color fields required.
html.pre: | eval clusterGroup=case( region="northeast", "servers", region="westcoast", "routers", region="midwest", "switches", 1=1, "firewalls" ) | table latitude, longitude, clusterGroup
html.p: The map to the right shows four groups spread across the US, each rendered in its assigned color. Zoom in to see individual markers — clusters dissolve and re-form as you zoom.

search.query: | makeresults count=120 | streamstats count as i | eval region=case(i<=30,"northeast",i<=60,"westcoast",i<=90,"midwest",1=1,"southeast") | eval latitude=case(region="northeast",40.7+(i%7-3)*0.45,region="westcoast",37.5+(i%7-3)*0.7,region="midwest",41.8+(i%7-3)*0.45,1=1,32.0+(i%7-3)*0.7) | eval longitude=case(region="northeast",-74.0+(i%5-2)*0.45,region="westcoast",-121.0+(i%5-2)*0.7,region="midwest",-87.6+(i%5-2)*0.45,1=1,-83.5+(i%5-2)*0.7) | eval clusterGroup=case(region="northeast","servers",region="westcoast","routers",region="midwest","switches",1=1,"firewalls") | table latitude, longitude, clusterGroup

html.p: Add clusterBgColor and/or clusterFgColor to your SPL results to override the formatter color at query time. Useful when color is data-driven — for example, coloring by environment, severity, or ownership.
In this example the formatter declares assets_prod:#E74C3C (red), but the SPL query adds purple override fields. The clusters render purple — SPL always wins.
html.pre: | eval clusterGroup="assets_prod" | eval clusterBgColor="#9B59B6" | eval clusterFgColor="#6C3483" | table latitude, longitude, clusterGroup, clusterBgColor, clusterFgColor
html.p: Tip: if only one field is present the other mirrors it, so clusterBgColor alone is sufficient when you want a flat color.

search.query: | makeresults count=50 | streamstats count as i | eval latitude=41.8+(i%7-3)*0.45 | eval longitude=-87.6+(i%6-3)*0.45 | eval clusterGroup="assets_prod" | eval clusterBgColor="#9B59B6" | eval clusterFgColor="#6C3483" | table latitude, longitude, clusterGroup, clusterBgColor, clusterFgColor

html.h3: 3 — Color Formats, default Fallback & Contrast Labels
html.p: clusterGroupColors accepts any valid CSS color. Three formats are supported:
The reserved key default acts as a catch-all — any clusterGroup value not explicitly listed in the mapping will fall back to it.

Contrast labels: dark_hosts uses a near-black color (#1A252F). The cluster count label automatically switches to white for legibility. The unknown_group markers in the Southeast have no explicit mapping and fall through to the default purple.

search.query: | makeresults count=100 | streamstats count as i | eval region=case(i<=25,"northeast",i<=50,"westcoast",i<=75,"midwest",1=1,"southeast") | eval latitude=case(region="northeast",40.7+(i%7-3)*0.45,region="westcoast",37.5+(i%6-3)*0.5,region="midwest",41.8+(i%7-3)*0.45,1=1,32.0+(i%6-3)*0.5) | eval longitude=case(region="northeast",-74.0+(i%5-2)*0.45,region="westcoast",-122.0+(i%5-2)*0.5,region="midwest",-87.6+(i%5-2)*0.45,1=1,-84.0+(i%5-2)*0.5) | eval clusterGroup=case(region="northeast","dark_hosts",region="westcoast","staging",region="midwest","cdn",1=1,"unknown_group") | table latitude, longitude, clusterGroup
